conclusion: Two C282Y alleles: the genotype in roughly 80-90% of clinically diagnosed HFE haemochromatosis. Penetrance is incomplete and strongly modified by sex, age, alcohol and blood loss, so this is a susceptibility genotype rather than a diagnosis.

One C282Y and one H63D, in trans — no wild-type HFE protein on either chromosome. A recognised at-risk genotype: mildly raised transferrin saturation and ferritin in a minority, and clinical iron overload only with a co-factor. Distinct from carrying both variants on one chromosome.

Both variants on one chromosome and an intact HFE on the other. The same two alleles as the compound heterozygote and NOT the same finding: one wild-type copy remains, so the expectation is that of a simple C282Y carrier.
A single C282Y allele. Carrier; iron indices are usually normal and clinical iron overload is not expected from this genotype alone.
Two H63D alleles. Not an established cause of iron overload on its own; reported iron indices largely overlap the general population.
A single H63D allele. Common in the general population and not informative on its own.

phenotype: C282Y/H63D in cis with a second C282Y
conclusion: Two C282Y alleles plus an H63D in cis with one of them. Functionally the C282Y homozygote; the additional H63D is on a chromosome that already carries C282Y.
Neither common HFE allele. Does not exclude rarer HFE variants or non-HFE iron overload.
